stimulus.source_note: Uncle Sam’s Youngest Son, Citizen Know Nothing (Sarony & Co., lithograph, New York, 1854). Library of Congress, LCCN2003689281. Public domain.
stimulus.text: A lithograph published in New York in 1854, titled “Uncle Sam’s Youngest Son, Citizen Know Nothing.” It shows a young man in a wide-brimmed hat, wrapped in an American flag, with a plaque reading “CITIZEN” below him and an eagle above.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Know-Nothing leaders most directly sought to

options.text: restrict immigration and keep recent immigrants from voting.
abolish slavery in the District of Columbia.
options.misconception: Background from the books: ending slavery in the capital was an abolitionist demand; Know-Nothings aimed their energy at immigrants, not at slavery.

options.text: open the West to small free farmers.
options.misconception: Background from the books: opening Western land to small farmers was the free-soil idea; the Know-Nothings fought over who could vote, not over Western land.

options.text: extend voting rights to all adult men.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Know-Nothings wanted fewer voters, not more; they sought longer waits before immigrants could vote.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the party’s program was restriction: fewer immigrants admitted, and longer waits before newcomers could vote.
rationales.B: Background from the books: ending slavery in the capital was an abolitionist demand; Know-Nothings aimed their energy at immigrants, not at slavery.
rationales.C: Background from the books: opening Western land to small farmers was the free-soil idea; the Know-Nothings fought over who could vote, not over Western land.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the Know-Nothings wanted fewer voters, not more; they sought longer waits before immigrants could vote.
rationales.general:
1. Name the party’s enemy: the newly arrived immigrant, especially the Catholic.
2. Background from the books: Know-Nothings tried to restrict further immigration and to keep recent immigrants from voting.
3. Test the options: only restriction matches a party built on keeping newcomers out of power and out of the voting booth.
Remember: a party’s program follows its fear; find the fear first.
